claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is a single-phase BCC or near-BCC solid solution.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has established high strength over a wide temperature range.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high-temperature phase stability.
A fraction of Ta should be replaced with Nb, with HfMoTa(Nb0.2Ta0.8)TiZr offered as an example target composition.
Partial Nb substitution for Ta will reduce the alloy density.
Partial Nb substitution for Ta will retain room-temperature mechanical properties.
Partial Nb substitution for Ta will retain mechanical properties at elevated temperatures up to approximately 1000 °C.
The Nb substitution will be uniformly accommodated while retaining a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Retention of the BCC solid solution will preserve solid-solution strengthening.
Nb has a lower atomic mass than Ta.
Replacing Ta with lower-mass Nb lowers average atomic mass and consequently lowers density.
Nb and Ta are chemically similar.
The chemical similarity of Nb and Ta will minimize disruption of the BCC lattice.
Minimal disruption of the BCC lattice will maintain phase stability and high-temperature mechanical properties.
The modified alloy will show a moderate density decrease while maintaining yield strength, ductility, and high-temperature resistance comparable to the baseline.
The proposed effect applies to standard-cast material under quasi-static loading at room temperature and around 1000 °C.
An optimized Nb substitution ratio can keep the alloy single-phase and stable during high-temperature exposure.
The optimum Nb substitution level is unknown and requires systematic experimental optimization.

contradictions.description: The literal target formula HfMoTa(Nb0.2Ta0.8)TiZr contains both a full Ta term and an additional Ta-rich mixed term. Read literally, it increases rather than partially replaces the Ta fraction, conflicting with the stated intervention. The likely intended formula is HfMo(Nb0.2Ta0.8)TiZr.

The predicted outcome says mechanical properties will be maintained or comparable, whereas the rejection rule accepts reductions of up to 10%. Thus, a measurable sacrifice in properties could be accepted despite the stated maintenance claim.
